text:
Ethan Park: We need to lock down the override path for guardrails gating. Questions:
1) who can override (RBAC role(s))
2) what do we capture as justification
3) do we require a second approver, and for which tiers/change types?

Jordan Lee: +1. Also need to be explicit if override is “apply anyway” vs “apply with manual approval required” (i.e., in-policy vs out-of-policy).

Benji Okafor: Current thought from ENG-3920 was `override_with_justification` behind feature flag. But we didn’t settle the permission model.

Naomi Feldman: From audit/RBAC side, we need:
- requester identity
- approver identity (if different)
- justification text + link to ticket/incident (strongly preferred)
- what exactly was overridden (policy version, suite id, failing metrics)
- reason category (enum) so we can report on it without reading free-form

Sean Gallagher: SRE view: if this is too heavyweight, oncall will just ping someone to disable gating. We should make override easy but controlled. Suggest:
- allow override only for `platform_oncall` and `support_escalation` (maybe) roles
- require a ticket link (PagerDuty incident / Jira / Linear) for anything in hard-block

Marcus Lin: Security concern is “silent bypass.” If override exists, it needs a second set of eyes at least for enterprise/private tenants. Otherwise this will become the default.

Paula Mendes: On the pilot calls, customers asked “who can bypass quality checks” and “can we prove it didn’t happen.” So I’m on board with strict auditability. But double-approval on every override might be too slow.

Ethan Park: Proposed split:
- Observe-only: no override concept (just logging)
- Soft-block: user can request override; requires approver with permission
- Hard-block (GA): overrides still possible but constrained

Jordan Lee: Let’s define two actions:
- `guardrails.override.request`
- `guardrails.override.approve`
Then we can set policy: some roles can request but only a smaller set can approve.

Benji Okafor: Implementation wise in control plane, easiest is:
- request includes `justification`, `reason_code`, `ticket_url`
- approval writes an `override_grant` object with TTL and “single-use” semantics
But note: our doc store schema shouldn’t become nested, just fields.

Naomi Feldman: Whatever we do, “single-use” is key. Overrides should not become a standing exception. Also we need to prevent PII in justification (people paste customer snippets).

Marcus Lin: +1 on PII. Can we enforce a warning + regex block for obvious patterns (emails, phone numbers)? At least add a UI banner “Don’t include customer data.”

Sean Gallagher: For runtime reality: high priority customer might need a config change now. Waiting for a second approver in the middle of an incident could be painful. Can we do:
- 1 approver for Dedicated/Hosted
- 2 approvers for Private (and maybe Enterprise tier?)

Paula Mendes: Maybe make 2-person approval only for certain optimization types (quantization) since that’s where we’ve seen the biggest quality hits.

Ethan Park: That feels right. Quantization overrides are the scary ones.

Jordan Lee: We can encode this in policy engine: `override_requirements` based on `change_type` + `tenant_tier`.
Example:
- quantization + enterprise/private => 2 approvers
- batching/caching/routing + enterprise => 1 approver
- any + self-serve => no override (blocked)

Benji Okafor: Wait, “no override for self-serve” meaning even internal Redwood users can’t override? Or only external? We’ll need a concept of “tenant tier” + “actor type”.

Naomi Feldman: External self-serve should not have override. For internal operations we can gate behind `redwood_internal` claims.

Marcus Lin: Agree. External “bring your own prompts” doesn’t mean “bypass evals.”

Sean Gallagher: Another constraint: rate limit overrides per tenant. If we see >N overrides/week, it should page or at least alert.

Ethan Park: Good. Something like 3/week/tenant for enterprise, 0 for self-serve. Plus dashboard panel.

Jordan Lee: On “justification,” we should make it structured:
- reason_code enum: `INCIDENT_MITIGATION`, `CUSTOMER_BLOCKED`, `FALSE_POSITIVE_SUSPECTED`, `EVAL_INFRA_OUTAGE`, `OTHER`
- freeform `justification` min length (say 30 chars)
- required `ticket_url` except maybe `EVAL_INFRA_OUTAGE`? (but even then should link to incident)

Benji Okafor: We can enforce required `ticket_url` always. Even “OTHER” can be a Linear task.

Paula Mendes: UX note: don’t show “override” label to customers. In Console, for allowed tenants, call it “Request manual approval” and “Approved by Redwood operator” (or customer admin if we allow that later).

Naomi Feldman: Careful: if customer admins can approve, audit log still needs to capture that identity. But for v1 I’d prefer Redwood-only approvers.

Marcus Lin: Redwood-only approvers reduces risk, yes.

Sean Gallagher: +1. If customer wants self-approval, they can disable Optimize applies and do config themselves.

Ethan Park: So v1: only Redwood roles can approve. Customers can *request* (enterprise), but approval is by Redwood oncall/escalation.

Jordan Lee: What about second approver mechanics? We can do:
- approval step 1 creates `override_pending_second_approval` state
- approval step 2 finalizes and issues `override_grant`
TTL 30 min; single-use; scope to the exact proposed change hash.

Benji Okafor: Scoping to exact change hash is important. Otherwise someone could approve and then apply a different delta.

Naomi Feldman: +100. Audit event should include `config_delta_digest` (hash) and the system should reject if it doesn’t match.

Marcus Lin: Also include `policy_version` and `prompt_set_revision` and `eval_run_id` that was evaluated.

Ethan Park: That all goes into the OptimizeConfigChange audit event (PR_18481). We’ll add override fields:
- `override_requested` bool
- `override_reason_code`
- `override_justification`
- `override_ticket_url`
- `override_approved_by` (list?)

Benji Okafor: For 2 approvers, audit wants an array. But our event pipeline can store a delimited string if needed. e.g. `override_approved_by="naomi;sean"`.

Naomi Feldman: That’s fine as long as we define it. Also: store `override_approved_at` timestamps? If we can’t do list/timestamps cleanly, at least store both approver ids and the final approval time.

Jordan Lee: Policy engine can treat “approver_2” as optional; but when required it must be non-empty.

Sean Gallagher: Operationally, who are the approvers?
- `platform_oncall` (SRE / platform)
- `security_oncall`? maybe only for Private?

Marcus Lin: I don’t want security as a required path for every quantization override (we’ll get paged constantly). But for Private tier, 2 approvers could be `platform_oncall` + `ml_evals_oncall` instead.

Paula Mendes: ML-evals oncall isn’t staffed 24/7 right now though.

Sean Gallagher: Exactly. Nights/weekends will be blocked.

Ethan Park: Let’s set required approvers by role, not by team:
- approver #1 must have `guardrails.override.approve`
- approver #2 must have `guardrails.override.approve_secondary`
We can grant secondary to a smaller set (platform leads + maybe security), but ensure at least one person in each region/timezone.

Naomi Feldman: That’s workable. Also ensures separation of duties.

Connor O'Brien: (dropping in) Release train concern: we should ship with 1-approver everywhere initially, then enable 2-approver via feature flag once roles are assigned and documented. Otherwise we’ll stall GA.

Ethan Park: +1. Plan:
- Pilot: 1-approver for all enterprise design partners; quantization still allowed but logged heavily
- Pre-GA: add secondary approver capability + RBAC roles
- GA: turn on 2-approver requirement for quantization overrides on enterprise/private

Marcus Lin: OK if we have a deadline to flip it for GA. We should treat “1 approver for quant overrides” as temporary.

Sean Gallagher: Works for me. Also need a runbook section: “how to approve override”, “when not to approve”, and “post-override follow-up”.

Paula Mendes: Post-override follow-up should include rerunning eval suite with higher sample size, and setting a reminder to remove the override. Maybe add a required checkbox “rerun scheduled” in UI.

Benji Okafor: If we do single-use + TTL, there’s nothing to “remove”, but we can require a follow-up task link.

Naomi Feldman: + add a required field `follow_up_ticket_url`? Might be overkill. Let’s keep one ticket URL and require it to track follow-up.

Jordan Lee: Summarizing decisions (unless objections):
- Override exists only for enterprise/private tenants (no self-serve override).
- Two-step model: request + approve.
- Approve requires `guardrails.override.approve` permission.
- For quantization on enterprise/private: add optional 2nd approver capability now; enforce via flag at GA.
- Override grant is single-use, scoped to `config_delta_digest`, TTL 30 min.
- Required fields on request: reason_code enum, justification (min length), ticket_url.
- Audit log must include: policy_version, eval_run_id, prompt_set_revision, failing metrics summary, digest, requester + approver(s).

Ethan Park: Sounds good. I’ll translate this into the RBAC/override section for ENG-3920 + ping Naomi for audit field names. :thumbsup:

Marcus Lin: Please add explicit “No customer data in justification” warning + redaction guidance.

Naomi Feldman: I’ll add the audit spec delimited format for multiple approvers. Also want a metric: `guardrails_override_total{reason_code,tenant_tier,change_type}` (sampling ok).

Sean Gallagher: And rate limit + alert when overrides spike. I’ll file a follow-up for dashboards.

Paula Mendes: Cool. I’ll update the pilot comms so CSMs don’t promise customer self-approval.
